# John Ashdown

- **Age:** Middle-aged  <sub>[v5 c2 P8](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0008), [v5 c13 P11](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0011), [v5 c21 P8](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0008)</sub>

- **Origin:** Juneford  <sub>[v5 c4 P57](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0057)</sub>
- **Role:** Presbyterian Minister  <sub>[v1 c21 P4](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0004), [v5 c2 P8](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0008)</sub>

## Appearance

John Ashdown is a tall man with an alabaster-like paleness, fine and delicate hands, and dark, visionary, handsome eyes. His dark hair is often unkempt and hangs in unbrushed locks across his high forehead. He has a pale, chiseled face, unwrinkled and handsome, though his clothes and carpet slippers are often untidy due to his absent-mindedness.

_Sources: [v5 c1 P6](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0006), [v5 c2 P3](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0003), [v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008), [v5 c5 P12](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0012), [v5 c13 P11](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0011), [v5 c14 P12](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0012), [v5 c14 P20](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0020), [v5 c14 P28](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0028)_

## Personality

John Ashdown is a scholarly, gentle, and deeply spiritual man who delivers eloquent and engaging sermons. He is remarkably absent-minded, impractical, and prone to losing himself in books, theoretical concepts, and reveries. Although he is shy around most women, he is deeply affectionate, lenient, and indulgent toward his children, hating to punish them. He possesses a subtle, hidden sense of humor and steel-like inner strength when provoked on matters of principle.

_Sources: [v1 c21 P5](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0005), [v5 c2 P8](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0008), [v5 c2 P11](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0011), [v5 c2 P47](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0047), [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001), [v5 c4 P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005), [v5 c13 P6](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0006), [v5 c13 P8](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0008), [v5 c14 P18](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0018), [v5 c14 P21](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0021)_

## History

John Ashdown previously served as a minister at Juneford, where his beloved wife, Cecilia, died shortly after giving birth to their youngest child, Ida. He was left a widower with four young children and the assistance of an elderly relative, Aunt Martha. He was called to Brierley and Glen St. Agnes to replace the retiring Mr. Bentley, where he won over the congregation with his engaging sermons, despite his impractical nature and absent-mindedness. For years, he remained consumed by grief for his late wife and struggled to manage his wild, motherless children. Eventually, he fell in love with Clementine Ainslie, an elegant parishioner from the hill. Although she initially rejected his proposal due to a secret oath made to her sister, her young stepdaughter-to-be, Ida, visited her and persuaded her to reconsider. Clementine accepted him, and their upcoming marriage brought immense joy and new order to his family.

## Quotes

> It is a sorrowful deficiency—a most sorrowful deficiency. On multiple occasions, I have conversed with your father regarding this matter, dutifully highlighting his obligation to him, yet up to now it has yielded no result.  <sub>[v5 c14 P17](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0017)</sub>

> Mrs. Twiss, I am grateful for your good intentions, nevertheless, my child cannot be given to you.  <sub>[v5 c14 P21](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0021)</sub>

> That will suffice, woman! I wish to listen to nothing further, Mrs. Twiss. You have spoken excessively.  <sub>[v5 c14 P29](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0029)</sub>

> My principle, Edmund, is, refrain from fighting until you are certain that you should, and after that apply every bit of your strength to it.  <sub>[v5 c17 P63](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0063)</sub>

> You see, my thoughts were on the way I could make things better for them, and my hope is that my actions will succeed.  <sub>[v5 c21 P6](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0006)</sub>
